question: Do Vietnamese consumers accept a sausage, giò lụa or dumpling filling in which 20 to 30 percent of the meat is replaced by a fungal or fermented protein, at the same price and protein level, in a blind test?
why_it_matters: This is the most likely entry route and no Vietnamese tasting data exist. A single central-location test would move the evidence from stated to tested.
cheapest_way_to_close: Blind central-location test with 100 to 150 consumers in Hanoi and Ho Chi Minh City using existing processor recipes; a university sensory lab can run it for a few thousand USD.
owner_org_to_ask: HUST School of Biotechnology and Food Technology (authors of RD-32 and NOV-02); Nha Trang University; a processor such as Vissan or CJ Foods Vietnam

question: Which Vietnamese name for cultivated meat is least damaging: thịt nuôi cấy, thịt tế bào, thịt nhân tạo, or a benefit phrase?
why_it_matters: Press uses thịt nhân tạo (artificial) for both plant-based and cell-based products, and 'fake food' scandals are live. Names change acceptance in other markets.
cheapest_way_to_close: Add a randomised name-and-frame module to any planned online survey (n about 1000); cost is low if added to an existing omnibus.
owner_org_to_ask: Q&Me, Decision Lab or Cimigo omnibus; SMU team behind NOV-32 for method

question: What share of each country's sample, including Vietnam, fell into each segment in Lin et al. 2026, and what exact adoption-readiness items were used?
why_it_matters: It is the only multi-country Asian study with Vietnamese cultivated meat data; we could read only the abstract.
cheapest_way_to_close: Email the corresponding author for the country table.
owner_org_to_ask: Bioeconomy Science Institute, New Zealand (Mao-Tang Lin)

question: What are the Vietnam-only (Ho Chi Minh City) results of GFI APAC's Decoding Demand survey, including sample size and the blended-meat question wording?
why_it_matters: The 93 percent blended figure is regional and stated; the Vietnam breakout and exact wording decide how much weight it can carry.
cheapest_way_to_close: Download the gated report with a registration, or ask GFI APAC for the Vietnam slide.

question: Will precision-fermented proteins that contain no DNA have to carry a GMO (biến đổi gen) label on consumer products under Decree 43/2026 and the new Food Safety Law?
why_it_matters: A GMO label is a strong negative in Vietnam (84 percent premium for non-GM soymilk; non-GMO claims by VitaDairy and Vinasoy). The answer decides whether PF can go direct to consumers or only B2B.
cheapest_way_to_close: Written query to the regulator; review the draft Food Safety Law text when tabled in October to November 2026.
owner_org_to_ask: Vietnam Food Administration (Ministry of Health); Ministry of Agriculture and Environment

question: How much lactoferrin (and whey protein isolate) do Vietnamese formula and nutrition makers import each year, at what price, and would they accept a precision-fermented source?
why_it_matters: Lactoferrin is the clearest premium PF ingredient and VitaDairy, Nutifood and Morinaga already market it in Vietnam; volume and price set the addressable B2B market.
cheapest_way_to_close: Customs data query by HS code plus two procurement interviews.
owner_org_to_ask: VitaDairy, Nutifood, Vinamilk procurement; Vietnam Dairy Association; Vietnam customs data

question: What is the soy protein and other functional protein inclusion rate in Vietnamese processed meats, and what price per kg do processors pay for these proteins?
why_it_matters: It defines the existing B2B slot that fungal or fermented proteins could take and the price to beat.
cheapest_way_to_close: Two to three interviews with processor R&D managers; ingredient distributor price lists.
owner_org_to_ask: Vissan, CJ Foods Vietnam, SG Food, Cholimex; ingredient distributors

question: Is GOOD Meat 3 still on sale at Huber's Butchery, and what volumes and repeat purchases did it achieve?
why_it_matters: It is the only retail cultivated product in Asia; its fate is the best revealed test of consumer pull.
cheapest_way_to_close: Email Huber's Butchery and Eat Just; check shelf in person in Singapore.

question: How many of Vow's Singapore restaurant partners kept Forged on the menu after launch, and what were repeat orders?
why_it_matters: Dish counts are company claims without retention data; retention is the demand signal that matters.
cheapest_way_to_close: Ask Vow; call a sample of listed Singapore restaurants.

question: What happened to Vinh Hoan's stakes in Avant Meats and Shiok Meats and to Minh Phu's R&D MOU with Shiok Meats?
why_it_matters: They are the only Vietnamese corporate demand signals for cultivated seafood; their status shows whether incumbents still see value.
cheapest_way_to_close: Check Vinh Hoan annual reports and investor presentations; email investor relations.
owner_org_to_ask: Vinh Hoan Corporation; Minh Phu Seafood; Umami Bioworks

question: Would the Vietnam Buddhist Sangha or leading chay restaurants regard cultivated meat or precision-fermented dairy as chay?
why_it_matters: Chay consumers are the largest group already buying meat substitutes; a negative view would close that segment for cultivated products.
cheapest_way_to_close: Interview two or three senior monastics and chay restaurant owners; review Sangha publications.
owner_org_to_ask: Vietnam Buddhist Sangha; Au Lac and other chay brands

question: Does the word lên men (fermented) on a protein product raise acceptance compared with vi sinh (microbial), nấm men (yeast) or công nghệ sinh học (biotechnology)?
why_it_matters: Fermentation looks like a positive frame in Vietnamese media and marketing but has not been tested on protein labels.
cheapest_way_to_close: Add a four-arm label test to the naming survey above.
owner_org_to_ask: Same survey provider as the naming test

question: What is Vietnam's actual edible mushroom output: about 250,000 t or about 25,000 t per year?
why_it_matters: The two figures differ tenfold; the size of the mushroom habit and of substrate supply depend on it.
cheapest_way_to_close: Ask the Ministry of Agriculture and Environment crop department; check FAOSTAT for Vietnam.
owner_org_to_ask: Ministry of Agriculture and Environment; FAO

question: What volume of processed meats (xúc xích, giò chả, chả lụa, nuggets) does Vietnam produce and eat per year?
why_it_matters: Needed to size the blend route; we found no figure.
cheapest_way_to_close: Statistics office industrial output tables; processor annual reports.
owner_org_to_ask: National Statistics Office; Vissan and Masan MEATLife annual reports

question: Would Malaysian or Indonesian buyers accept a halal-certified blended or fermented protein made in Vietnam?
why_it_matters: Export demand for halal proteins could matter more than domestic demand for some products.
cheapest_way_to_close: Two importer interviews; check JAKIM and BPJPH rules for foreign-made novel proteins.
owner_org_to_ask: JAKIM; BPJPH Indonesia; Vietnam halal certifiers
